scenario.briefing: The campus bookstore exports stock as item records. Build a restock list for the warehouse without mutating the records.

title: Data classes and report pipelines
summary: Model stock records with an immutable data class, then build a sorted restock list and diagnose an inclusive boundary.

objectives.description: Build a collection pipeline over immutable records.
Find an inclusive comparison that overstocks the warehouse.
Transfer the pipeline to a total-units calculation.

hints: A data class generates equals, hashCode, toString, and copy from its constructor properties.
filter keeps the items below the threshold.
map turns each remaining Item into its name.
Chain filter, map, and sorted, then return the result.

misconceptions.description: Returning names in input order instead of sorted order.
misconceptions.testDescription: The pipeline filters low stock, maps names, and sorts them.
misconceptions.feedback: The warehouse reads the list alphabetically. Call sorted() after map so the output does not depend on input order.

misconceptions.description: Declaring record properties with var and mutating them in place.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Declaring data class properties with var and changing the record during the report.
misconceptions.feedback: Keep report records immutable with val. Build a new list instead of editing the source records.

misconceptions.description: Trying to fix a boundary error by sorting first.
misconceptions.feedback: Sorting changes presentation, not which items pass the filter. Correct the comparison operator.

misconceptions.description: Counting low-stock rows instead of summing their units.
misconceptions.feedback: count() counts records; sumOf { it.units } adds the units those records contain.

sections.title: Data classes describe records
sections.body: A data class such as data class Item(val name: String, val units: Int) is a concise record. The compiler generates equals, hashCode, toString, copy, and component functions from the constructor properties. val makes each property read-only, so a report never mutates the exported rows. copy creates a changed duplicate: item.copy(units = 0). Destructuring reads the generated components: val (name, units) = item.

sections.title: Pipelines read top to bottom
sections.body: Collection operators return new collections. filter keeps matching elements, map transforms each element, sorted returns an ascending list, and sumOf adds a selected number. A chain such as items.filter { it.units < threshold }.map { it.name }.sorted() states the report in the order it happens. Operators do not change the source list.

sections.title: Nullability inside records
sections.body: A property can be nullable, and a lookup can return null. mapNotNull drops null results, firstOrNull stops at the first match, and the Elvis operator ?: supplies a fallback. Keep absence visible in the type instead of forcing a value with !!.

steps.title: Build the restock list
steps.prompt: Edit Main.kt. restockNeeded returns the names of items whose units are below the threshold, in alphabetical order.
hints: Keep the data class and the List<Item> parameter.
Filter first so only low-stock records remain.
Map each remaining record to its name.
Sort the names before returning them.

steps.title: The inclusive boundary
steps.prompt: The warehouse says it is overstocking items that are exactly at the threshold. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: The report should include only items that need restocking.
An item at the threshold is not below it.
Read the comparison operator in the filter.
steps.explanation: A stock of exactly the threshold is still acceptable, so the restock condition is strictly less than. Reversing the operator selects the wrong half of the data.

steps.title: Total only the low-stock units
steps.prompt: A teammate needs the total number of units across items below the threshold. Which expression returns that total?
hints: Keep the low-stock filter from the report.
Totals add units, not names or row counts.
sumOf selects a number from each remaining record.

quiz.prompt: A teammate needs the total number of units across items below the threshold. Which expression returns that total?
quiz.explanation: The filter keeps the low-stock records, and sumOf { it.units } adds the unit count from each one. Summing every item includes stock that does not need a restock.
